title: Nmap's Debut in Phrack and the Open-Tool-Sharing Tradition (1997)
explainer: Nmap, one of the most widely used open-source security scanners, didn't start as a polished product: Gordon Lyon, writing under the pseudonym Fyodor, first published it with its source code included in the hacker zine Phrack in 1997, then grew it into a community-shaped, openly licensed project over the following decades. It's a concrete precedent for what this lesson asks of you: releasing working, inspectable code into the community so other researchers can audit, extend, and improve it rather than keep it closed.
